newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Thousands march in Philippine May Day protests.
newsitem.headline: Thousands march in Philippine May Day protests.

text.p: About 30,000 workers marched in Manila and other Philippine cities on Thursday as the country's squabbling unions marked May Day with demands for higher wages.
Police tightened security at power plants and other vital facilities north of Manila in the wake of intelligence reports that communist guerrillas planned to sabotage them, but there was no violence.

About 5,000 workers belonging to rival leftist unions marched to the presidential palace and nearly came to blows in a quarrel over which of them should be at the front of the protest. Their leaders separated the two groups after a shouting match.
The workers demanded a 100-peso increase in the daily wage, currently pegged at 180 pesos.
The biggest protest took place in central Bacolod city where 20,000 workers marched to demand higher wages.
Several thousand others participated in protests in central Luzon island, north of Manila.
President Fidel Ramos led official May Day celebrations by signing a law increasing the pensions of hundreds of thousands of workers in private firms covered by a state-operated pension fund.
Officials said Ramos had planned to announce approval of another law granting a tax exemption of 146,000 pesos ($5,550) to each low-income family with at least six children.
But the measure, approved by the House of Representatives on Wednesday, was stalled in the Senate.
"I call on both houses (of Congress) to fast-track the passing of the tax reform package which is expected to impact significantly on our ordinary workers," Ramos said in a speech.
